summary_hint: IRS <transcript_type> for <taxpayer_name> (TIN <taxpayer_tin_masked>), tax year <tax_period_ending>, filing <filing_status>: AGI <adjusted_gross_income>, taxable income <taxable_income>, total tax <total_tax>.

typed_core.name: transcript_type
typed_core.why: disambiguator — Return Transcript vs Tax Account vs Record of Account vs Wage & Income vs Verification of Nonfiling; each carries different data
typed_core.prompt_hint: Identify the transcript type first — it determines which fields exist; a Wage & Income transcript has no AGI/taxable-income line

typed_core.name: tax_period_ending
typed_core.why: identity — the tax year the transcript covers

typed_core.name: request_or_processing_date
typed_core.why: recency — when the transcript was pulled

typed_core.name: return_received_or_processed_date
typed_core.why: processor — when the IRS processed the return

typed_core.name: taxpayer_tin_masked
typed_core.prompt_hint: The TIN is already IRS-masked (XXX-XX-1234); do not attempt to reconstruct it

typed_core.name: spouse_name
typed_core.why: identity — joint filer; match to co-borrower

typed_core.name: customer_file_number
typed_core.why: identity — the lender's file-linkage number (10-digit CFN on IRS transcripts)
typed_core.prompt_hint: The 10-digit CFN the lender put on the 4506-C, echoed on the transcript — use it for file linkage, not the masked SSN

nested_lists.name: return_line_items
nested_lists.shape_reason: the transcript is a long list of labeled dollar lines (income items, adjustments, deductions, credits, per-computer values); many items → flat rows keep well under the 16,384-token ceiling

fields.name: section
fields.why: tags Income vs Adjustments vs Tax

fields.name: amount
fields.why: the line amount; supports future income-reconciliation rules

rejected.name: form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: the transcript layout is not a filled-form schema; tax_form_number covers the return form

rejected.name: document_issue_date, effective_date, expiration_date
rejected.reason: duplicate request/processing dates; a transcript does not expire

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block
rejected.reason: a transcript is agency-issued, not executed

rejected.name: wages_and_income_summary, account_adjustments, penalties_interest_and_payments
rejected.reason: rolled into the single return_line_items nested list (one-list budget)

encoding_variations: transcript_type — the five IRS products differ sharply: a Return Transcript has line items; a Tax Account Transcript has adjustments/payments; a Record of Account combines both; Wage & Income lists W-2/1099s; Verification of Nonfiling has no return data. The type governs which typed fields will be null
per-computer values — transcripts print both as-filed and 'PER COMPUTER' figures; prefer as-filed unless the rule says otherwise; note which was read
masked TIN — always 'XXX-XX-' + last 4; already masked by the IRS

open_questions.q: No attached rule — the packet lists 0 rules, yet IN-12 (self-employment) and income rules typically consume 1040 transcripts
options: design to identity/processor as done and flag that the rule mapping is incomplete
open_questions.recommendation: (a) design to identity/processor and surface the gap

open_questions.q: Which object[] is the nested list — return_line_items, wages_and_income_summary, and account_adjustments are all repeating
options: one flat return_line_items with a section tag absorbing all three
open_questions.recommendation: (a) one flat return_line_items; a Wage & Income transcript may warrant its own list if a rule reads per-payer income

options: type both if a rule cross-checks
open_questions.recommendation: confirm which figure the income analysis should trust; consider typing both if a rule cross-checks
